title: Material multipliers in manufactured products
method: Divide each finished cost or selling price by the material benchmark its source reports. Different cost boundaries and evidence types are explicit. No ratio is an industry-average manufacturing-efficiency measure or automatically removable-cost fraction.

cases.material_share_interpretation: No retained-material share is reported: this source does not provide an independently audited constituent-material inventory.
cases.figure_source: Fabricated cost / steel stock · Rohini et al.
cases.material_quantity_basis: design weights of steel plate and rolled sections
cases.numerator_boundary: Modeled fabrication cost including steel material, fabrication processes and 5% overhead; baseline rolled-section design in Table 3.
cases.material_boundary: INR 235565 steel sections plus INR 162293 steel plate and connection plates. Industrial steel stock valued at assumed INR/kg rates. Not an elemental inventory.
cases.limitations: Small academic modeling study, not an observed supplier sale or industry average. Material-price provenance is weak. Ancillary materials and installation are not separately reconciled. Open water/process tank, not a pressurized or nuclear vessel. Other table columns have apparent unit-price inconsistencies; the chosen baseline cost sum is internally consistent.

sources.title: Rohini et al. (2015), A study on the optimization of rectangular steel storage tanks
sources.location: Table 3, printed p. 39298, PDF page 5; baseline Rolled Steel Sections column.

cases.material_share_interpretation: No retained-material share is reported: this source does not provide an independently audited constituent-material inventory.
cases.numerator_boundary: Average new passenger-car selling price, about USD8/lb; includes raw materials, manufacturing and processing, shipping, OEM profit and dealer markup.
cases.material_boundary: DOE reported average raw-material cost of USD0.60/lb, covering the car material mix rather than purchased components. Detailed procurement form and retained-versus-bought quantities are not disclosed.
cases.limitations: Historical aggregate estimate, not a current named-vehicle teardown. Source inputs rounded. Numerator is retail selling price rather than factory cost. No commodity-by-commodity bill or separately cited raw-material calculation in the passage. Uses paired dollar-per-pound figures; no whole-car bill derived from the passenger-inclusive vehicle weight.

sources.title: U.S. Department of Energy (2012), Report on the First Quadrennial Technology Review: Technology Assessments
sources.location: Current Lightweighting Technology, printed p. 25, PDF page 29, paragraph beginning with average passenger-car weight.

cases.material_share_interpretation: Do not interpret the reciprocal of this ratio as retained-material share: the reported steel quantity basis is undisclosed. CSV material_value_share_percent is intentionally blank.
cases.numerator_boundary: Approximately $13000 half-nozzle-jacket component cost reported by SpaceX analyst Lucas Hughes in a meeting described by Walter Isaacson.
cases.material_boundary: Approximately $200 steel cost stated by Elon Musk for the single-piece steel component in the same meeting.
cases.limitations: Not an audited bill of materials or invoice. Alloy, mass, steel pricing date, bought-stock versus retained-mass treatment, scrap credits, and full component accounting boundary are undisclosed. One identified component, not a rocket-engine or aerospace-industry average. Meeting followed the August 2021 Starship surge; exact meeting date is not stated.

sources.title: Walter Isaacson, Elon Musk (2023), Chapter 59, Starship Surge; publisher-authorized excerpt on Space.com, October 3, 2023
